name_en: Someii — steamed rice dyed yellow with gardenia seed, pressed thin and dried
summary_ja: 蒸したもち米をくちなしの実で黄色く染めてすりつぶし、小判形に薄くのばして干した携帯食。旧東海道瀬戸（現・藤枝市）の茶屋で戦国時代から売られ、足腰の疲れを取る食べ物として旅人に評判だったと伝わる。
summary_en: Steamed sticky rice is dyed yellow with gardenia seed, mashed, and pressed thin into a portable travel food. Sold at teahouses along the old Tokaido in present-day Fujieda since the Warring States era, it's said to have earned a reputation for easing travelers' tired legs.
source_title: 染飯 静岡県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Bokumeshi — mixed rice with simmered eel and burdock root
summary_ja: 蒸したウナギとささがきごぼうを煮て、炊きたてのごはんに混ぜ込む。太すぎて売り物にならなかったウナギを養鰻場の「木杭（ぼっくい）」でまかない飯にしたのが名の由来と伝わる、大井川流域の混ぜごはん。
summary_en: Steamed eel and shaved burdock are simmered together and folded into freshly cooked rice. Its name is said to trace to oversized eels unfit for sale, used in staff meals at eel farms along the Oi River — a mixed rice dish of the region.
source_title: ぼくめし 静岡県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
